projectContext.legalCaveat: This is an engineering compliance record and architecture recommendation, not legal advice.

projects.name: AndroidX CameraX and CameraPipe
projects.requiredReview: Retain copyright and licence notices, review NOTICE/third-party dependencies, and prefer published AndroidX artifacts over copied internals.
patterns: Immutable graph configuration separates streams, reprocessing inputs, postview, session parameters, default/required parameters, listeners and backend.
Graph/session ownership makes lifecycle and recreation explicit.
Device flags and quirks bound repeating-before-capture, abort, close, finalization and restart behavior.
Simulator and fake-backend support make graph behavior testable without hardware.
limitations: CameraPipe is an AndroidX internal/experimental implementation surface and API stability must be checked before direct dependency changes.
It does not provide the replacement app's RAW processing, storage policy or vendor-key semantics.

projects.name: GrapheneOS Camera
projects.requiredReview: Review copied-file history, AndroidX/internal API use, dependencies, retained notices and compatibility with the replacement app's Java architecture.
patterns: Close scarce ImageProxy resources immediately after extraction instead of holding them through storage IO.
Pipeline extraction, write and thumbnail stages while preserving one-write output semantics.
Use MediaStore pending/finalization, SAF, fsync where appropriate and deletion of incomplete outputs.
Keep EXIF/location disclosure and external capture-intent behavior explicit and privacy-first.
limitations: The app is Kotlin/CameraX-oriented and does not supply the target's portable RAW burst or vendor adapter.
Use of restricted AndroidX internals requires maintenance and dependency review.

projects.name: Open Camera
projects.licenseEvidence: official project licence and source headers
projects.requiredReview: Any code or dependency reuse requires a deliberate GPL-compatible distribution decision and an updated compliance register.
patterns: Broad Camera2 capability probing and user-visible fallback behavior.
RAW/DNG, focus and exposure bracketing, queued save work and bounded storage failures.
Device-specific quirk inventory and mature manual-control edge cases.
MediaStore/SAF selection and app-policy separation from the camera controller.
limitations: GPL-3.0-or-later code is not copied into the MIT project.
The large controller and application-policy surfaces should become independent tests and small contracts rather than a monolithic port.

projects.name: MotionCam
projects.requiredReview: No direct code or linked native component enters the MIT app without an explicit GPL-compatible distribution decision.
patterns: Explicit NDK camera event loop and capture/session error callbacks.
Bounded RAW buffer ownership with ready/unused queues and memory accounting.
Timestamp-selected buffer consumption and immutable locked buffer sets.
Background RAW capture and multi-frame processing separated from camera callbacks.
limitations: The native pipeline and algorithms are GPL-3.0-only and are requirements evidence only.
Hardware and memory assumptions must be re-measured on Galaga before implementing a buffer budget.

projects.name: PhotonCamera
projects.requiredReview: Repository-level GPL applies unless a specific file's complete provenance and compatible licence are independently established and approved.
patterns: Camera2 RAW_SENSOR and YUV_420_888 capture with explicit preview/capture states.
Frame-count selection and multi-frame processing executors.
Gyro sample collection and per-burst/per-frame deblur inputs.
Separate saver implementations and processing lifecycle.
limitations: Repository-level GPL means the implementation is not a direct reuse source for the MIT app.
Static globals, reflection/vendor helpers and a large controller are not adopted as architectural patterns.

projects.name: Libre Camera
projects.requiredReview: No Dart/Flutter source or GPL dependency is imported into the MIT app without a compatible distribution decision.
patterns: Compact privacy-first settings and optional EXIF behavior.
User-selected save location and common photo/video controls.
Clear UI-level feature and platform limitation communication.
limitations: Flutter camera abstraction does not meet the replacement app's direct Camera2, RAW burst, physical route or vendor-session needs.
GPL-3.0-only source is clean-room UI requirements evidence only.

recommendations.title: Align portable session plans with CameraPipe graph separation
requirements: Keep immutable stream, backend, binder, session parameter and request parameter scopes.
Expose graph state and listeners through portable interfaces rather than framework objects.
Do not replace the current engine wholesale or weaken vendor-adapter isolation.
recommendations.rationale: The existing session engine already matches the strongest CameraPipe separation and should evolve through small conformance improvements.

recommendations.title: Add graph and backend simulation tests
requirements: Simulate surface loss, session recreation, repeating-before-capture and backend failure events.
Verify each recovery path remains bounded and cancellation wins over retries.
Keep tests independent of Galaga hardware while reserving device validation for measured thresholds.
recommendations.rationale: CameraPipe's simulator pattern can increase deterministic coverage without importing Android framework objects into portable tests.

recommendations.title: Implement a staged privacy-first storage pipeline
requirements: Close Image/ImageProxy resources immediately after extracting owned bytes.
Write output once, fsync where appropriate, finalize pending MediaStore rows and delete incomplete outputs.
Support SAF and make EXIF/location disclosure explicit and private by default.
Classify extraction, creation, write, finalization and thumbnail failures separately.
recommendations.rationale: GrapheneOS provides a permissively licensed, production-oriented storage and privacy pattern aligned with the replacement app.

recommendations.title: Design a bounded RAW/YUV buffer pool independently
requirements: Bound frame count and memory bytes independently of producer speed.
Represent ownership transfer, ready/unused state, cancellation and backpressure explicitly.
Select frames only through request identity and normalized timestamp correlation.
Measure Galaga memory and throughput before setting production budgets.
recommendations.rationale: GPL projects demonstrate the operational need, but the implementation must be independently designed for the existing portable capture contracts.

recommendations.title: Add gyro snapshots keyed to the capture clock domain
requirements: Use a bounded monotonic gyro ring with immutable per-frame snapshots.
Record sensor timestamp source and normalize it before association.
Reject unknown clock domains, frame mismatch and out-of-tolerance samples before alignment.
Make gyro optional and disclose unsupported hardware or timing quality.
recommendations.rationale: PhotonCamera supplies concept evidence for gyro-assisted bursts, while the existing fail-closed timestamp contract defines the safe independent design.

recommendations.title: Convert mature Camera2 edge cases into independent tests
requirements: Add capability-probe, manual focus/exposure, RAW/DNG, bracketing, queue pressure, SAF and MediaStore failure cases.
Keep device quirks evidence-linked and isolated from generic policy.
Do not port the monolithic controller or GPL implementation.
recommendations.rationale: Open Camera's breadth is most valuable as a clean-room regression inventory rather than a source-code dependency.

recommendations.title: Use Libre Camera only as a clean-room UI/settings reference
requirements: Expose privacy defaults, save location, format, resolution, FPS, focus and exposure controls only when backend capabilities support them.
Keep unsupported multi-camera and manual controls visibly unavailable.
Do not adopt Flutter or its camera plugin as the replacement backend.
recommendations.rationale: The project is useful for compact UI and disclosure patterns but does not satisfy low-level capture requirements.

recommendations.title: Enforce a no-GPL-import default for the MIT application
requirements: Do not copy GPL-family code, generated output or linked native libraries into the MIT application by default.
Allow independently written requirements, tests and high-level architectural observations with source attribution.
Require an explicit distribution/licensing decision and compliance-register update before any exception.
recommendations.rationale: This preserves the current MIT distribution intent while allowing clean-room learning from GPL projects.

nonClaims: The review does not certify legal compliance for a future release.
A permissive licence does not approve wholesale copying without file-provenance and dependency review.
A GPL project's architecture does not become MIT-compatible merely because it is summarized.
The review does not prove Galaga supports RAW, reprocessing, auxiliary physical IDs or usable gyro synchronization.
The review does not replace target-device tests or the source/licence compliance register.

updateTriggers: An upstream revision or licence changes
A new source dependency or copied file is proposed
RAW, gyro or storage implementation is added
A release compliance review changes a reuse decision
